I would absolutely recommend to almost anyone. All of the things the developers have added in the Title Updates have really fleshed out the game and gave us content to enjoy up until the expansion in 2027.

The game is visually stunning and offers a gameplay loop that feels almost endless. There's a lot to dive into with all of the weapons, and the various amount of builds you can make with each of them. Many niches can be carved out with minor adjustments to your build that add a whole new element to each monster hunt. It's great to play on your own and a lot of fun to play with others. Try out the demo first for free and if you enjoy it buy the whole thing and get ready for the expansion in 2027!

Caveat's:
When it launched people did have performance/start-up issues at first. Luckily Capcom finally was able to make a fix and address most of those problems. I would be surprised if anyone was still having game ruining problems outside of outdated and below spec hardware at this point in time.

People are also currently complaining that the game is too easy, that is a lie. It's a song and dance this community has done for every Monster Hunter game in the franchise, just to be put in their place when the Title updates release. With the DLC around the corner in 2027, it will just get even harder, so we have a lot to look forward to! Ignore these kinds of people and just have fun!

Begin Traversal Cutscene:

*Fires Hook Slinger at material node*
Character A - *Adult Peanut Character Noises*
*Fires Hook Slinger at material node*
Character B - *Adult Peanut Character Noises*
*Fires Hook Slinger at material node*
*Fires Hook Slinger at material node*
Character A - *Adult Peanut Character Noises*

Do you get the picture?

Facetious bit aside, I do think this is a well-made game. A bit *too* well made, in fact. The areas are perfectly designed for your new mount companion to the point where traversing any other way introduces massive friction to the experience. Your handler takes every opportunity to remind you of either a mechanic that's constantly occurring in the background or an environmental feature that you'll see dozens of times over the course of your playthrough.

I'm not arguing that this game should play *exactly* like whatever your pet Monster Hunter title is. Iteration and incremental changes are commonplace across any longstanding franchise. On top of that, fans of any entry could tell you the pain points of their particular gem are, and how they wish things were different. However, there can be *too* much change between singular titles, a fact that should be quite apparent given the variance present across the last few entries in this franchise.

I've enjoyed my time thus far with this game, and plan to participate in the expansion when that finally releases. However, it will not be taking the place of my favorite Monster Hunter. There *are* things I like about it, but there are equally as many things that I don't. I dislike needing to hold a button to keep it at a standstill. It is my get-out-of-jail free card whenever I am caught out of place during a hunt.

In my opinion, the Monster Hunter formula works for a reason. Its punishing nature teaches players about its mechanics, and to beware the monsters they hunt. The act of hunting a monster is a skill that should be slowly refined as you progress through the story and rise in hunter rank. Learning to use the environment to your advantage falls in this same category, as does learning how best to navigate this environment. This game, however, is doing its best to do all this thinking for you, from telling you about environmental features you can interact with, to your mount that does all the traversal for you so you can look cool and take in the environment without thinking.

To summarize:

Likes:
- Interconnected World
- Dual-Weapon Loadouts
- Expanded Radial Menu

Dislikes:
- Emphasis on Weak Point targeting
- Overemphasis on using your Seikret
- The "Set Piece-ification" of Monsters

If you like the things I dislike, then I'm happy for you, and I'm glad you finally got a game in this series that you can enjoy. Unfortunately for me, I think this game will never eclipse my play time in Monster Hunter World.

I've been playing monhon since the ps2 and only skipped the Wii U era, though had to wait for quite a while until Steam Machine before grabbing this entry. It's good overall, but has its problems here and there as well. Some map layouts are pretty bad, some sidequests just don't respect your time at all, the weapons feel a little dumbed down and simplified, and most egregious of all... the main story.

Monhon doesn't often cover itself in glory when it comes to the main plot of the games. But, this might be the worst of all of them. Just about every character is actively bad - especially Nata. They even somehow managed to fumble Gemma, making her more annoying than endearing when she has her little bit of limelight midway into the narrative. The Handler is boring. The side characters are bland. I never skip as a policy, but I've never been more tempted.

When the first arc of the story finished, I groaned to find Nata still in my camp instead of back with his people where he belongs. They must hate him as much as I do, quickly sending him off to be a liaison rather than take him back as they should. God, I wish they'd take him back. And now we get to look forward to him as a Hunter all grown up in the DLC? Ugh. I half expected him to come back in an Arkveld fursuit after all of that cringe.

The plus? Gameplay is excellent generally (easy mode though it may be) - it's monhon and you know what you're getting. Prepare to lose a few hundred hours of your life grinding away for talismans and decorations. It runs great on Steam Machine. The wounds and focus mode gimmick is interesting enough (though, all that free damage feels a bit like cheating sometimes, especially if you ever manage to chain 4-5 instances of the focus strike attacks).

Everyone who's a monhun fan and wanted this game probably has it already by now, so this review feels a little pointless. But I just had to get it off my chest. This story is so bad. Even for monhun, it's bad. Do yourself a favour and hold down that skip button. I regretted not doing it.

Also, shoutout to the two other Lance mains that exist out there somewhere.

The beauty of the untamed world, the awe-inspiring presence of every monster, and the rich narrative depth come together seamlessly. Balanced by unforgettable characters and the irresistible thrill of the hunt, this is an absolute triumph.
I've had nothing but fun with my friends, and it has been streamlined in a lot of ways to make playing with friends and questing faster and easier in comparison to the other games, in my opinion.

Monster Hunter Wilds is an absolute triumph of creature design, visceral combat, and sprawling, living ecosystems. The sheer scale of the new biomes and the fluidity of the weapon movesets make every hunt an unforgettable spectacle.

However, the game suffers from severe performance issues that heavily impact the experience. On many systems, frame rate stutters, optimization hiccups, and muddy texture streaming drag down the immersion, making smooth gameplay a constant battle against the hardware.

Furthermore, the story is a dismal 2/10. The narrative drags on with uninspired dialogue, predictable twists, and bland characters that you will actively want to skip just to get back to the action.

Despite these heavy flaws in technical stability and storytelling, the core gameplay loop of hunting, crafting, and mastering your weapon is too exhilarating to put down.
